name: vscode-swift-format
description: Format Swift files with swift-format, on macOS, Windows, or Linux.
author: Heiko Panjas

swiftFormat.requireConfigurationFile.markdownDescription: Only format Swift files when a `.swift-format` configuration file is found for the document. Without a configuration file, swift-format silently applies its built-in defaults and can reformat a project in a style nobody chose. Set to `false` to format anyway, using those defaults. Where the file is looked for is controlled by `#swiftFormat.configurationSearchScope#`.

swiftFormat.configurationSearchScope.markdownDescription: How far up the directory tree to search for a `.swift-format` file, starting from the directory of the document being formatted.
enumDescriptions: Stop at the workspace folder root. A configuration outside the workspace is ignored.
Keep walking to the filesystem root, matching swift-format's own lookup. A configuration in a parent directory or your home directory will be used.

swiftFormat.offerToCreateConfigurationFi.markdownDescription: Offer a **Create .swift-format** action when no configuration file is found, which writes swift-format's own default configuration to the workspace folder root. The file is only ever written when you choose that action. Set to `false` for a plain warning with no write action.

swiftFormat.path.markdownDescription: The full path to the swift-format **executable itself**, including its filename — not the folder that contains it. For example `/usr/local/bin/swift-format` (macOS/Linux) or `C:\swift\bin\swift-format.exe` (Windows), not `/usr/local/bin`. When set, this exact executable is used and `#swiftFormat.useXcrun#` is ignored. Leave empty to search PATH, or use `xcrun` on macOS — see `#swiftFormat.useXcrun#`.

swiftFormat.useXcrun.markdownDescription: Whether to run swift-format via `xcrun swift-format`, using Xcode's toolchain. Requires Xcode or the Xcode Command Line Tools. Ignored when `#swiftFormat.path#` is set.
enumDescriptions: Use xcrun on macOS, and PATH everywhere else.
Always use xcrun. Fails on a platform without Xcode.
Never use xcrun; always search PATH instead.

swiftFormat.additionalArguments.markdownDescription: Extra arguments passed to `swift-format format`, appended after the arguments this extension builds itself (for example `--strict` or `--ignore-unparsable-files`). Quote an argument containing spaces, e.g. `--configuration "/path/with spaces/.swift-format"`. Because these are appended last, a repeated `--configuration` here overrides the one this extension found — but `--offsets` does not work the same way: swift-format treats repeated `--offsets` as additional ranges to format, not a replacement, so an `--offsets` here adds to a selection format rather than replacing it.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run lint && npm run compile
